name: Curupira
description: A forest-protector spirit of Tupi-Guaraní tradition in Brazil and neighbouring countries, depicted as a small, red-haired figure with backward-facing feet that punishes hunters who take more than they need and rewards those who respect the forest.
origin: Tupi-Guaraní cultural area: most of Brazil, with strong attestation in the Amazon basin, Atlantic forest, and Cerrado regions; cognate figures in Paraguay and the Guianas.
